```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Li et al. (2016) recovered the non-disclosed humanized IgG1 antibody MAB2
(Biogen) from patient serum by anti-idiotypic affinity purification,
profiled its post-translational modifications by peptide-mapping LC-MS, and
fitted a mechanistic PK model to two of them: deamidation of a conserved Fc
asparagine and the Man5 (mannose-5) Fc glycoform. The paper fits the same
four-state framework (Figure 5, Equations 1-4) separately to each
attribute, so the library carries two models that share this article:

* `Li_2016_MAB2_deamidation` -- the original form converts first-order to
  the deamidated form (`ktr`), in both the central and the peripheral
  compartment, and both forms are cleared at the same rate.
* `Li_2016_MAB2_man5` -- no conversion (`ktr = 0`); the Man5 glycoform is
  cleared faster than the rest of MAB2.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2016_MAB2_deamidation"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2016.1186322>

```{r models}
mod_deamid <- readModelDb("Li_2016_MAB2_deamidation")
mod_man5 <- readModelDb("Li_2016_MAB2_man5")
```

Both models are typical-value models. The coefficients of variation printed
in Table 1 are the precision of the parameter estimates (footnote to Table 1),
not between-subject variability, and the paper reports no residual error
model, so neither model carries an `eta` or a residual-error term.

Each model takes the dose in two records at the same time, one into
`central` and one into the modified-form central compartment
(`central_deamid` or `central_man5`), each carrying the **full** dose amount.
The bioavailability split `f(central) <- 1 - fdose_<attribute>` and
`f(central_<attribute>) <- fdose_<attribute>` reproduces the paper's two
inputs `AC0(0) = (1 - f) x Dose` and `ACmod(0) = f x Dose`. The initial
level `100 x f` is a property of the drug-product batch, so it is a fixed
`ini()` parameter that a user can override for another batch.

# Population

Three patients in a single-ascending-dose study each received the same
single high intravenous dose of MAB2 from one drug-product batch; the dose
amount, the indication and the patients' demographics are not reported.
Serum was sampled pre-dose, at 10 min, 1, 4 and 12 h, and on days 2, 4, 7,
14, 21 and 42 (Methods, "Clinical sample information"). Parameters were
estimated with ADAPT.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Li_2016_MAB2_deamidation")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Deamidation model | Man5 model | Source location |
|----------------------|-------------------|------------|-----------------|
| `lk12` (kCP, 1/day)  | log(0.17)  | log(0.18)  | Table 1 |
| `lk21` (kPC, 1/day)  | log(0.093) | log(0.096) | Table 1 |
| `lkmet_deamid` (ktr, 1/day) | log(0.01) | not present (ktr = 0) | Table 1; Methods assumption 2 |
| `lkel` (kcl0, 1/day) | log(0.13)  | log(0.127) | Table 1 |
| `kel_deamid` / `lkel_man5` (kclmod, 1/day) | `kel_deamid <- kel` (0.13) | log(0.295) | Table 1; Methods assumption 1 (deamidation does not change clearance) |
| `lvc` (V, L)          | log(3.34)  | log(3.32)  | Table 1 |
| `fdose_deamid` / `fdose_man5` | 0.056 (fixed) | 0.030 (fixed) | Table 2 and Figure 6 (initial level of the clinical batch; see Assumptions) |
| Central and peripheral ODEs, both forms | Eq. 1-4 | Eq. 1-4 with ktr = 0 | Methods, "Pharmacokinetic modeling"; Figure 5 |
| Dose split into the two forms | `f()` on both central states | same | Methods: `AC0(t=0) = (1 - f) x Dose`, `ACmod(t=0) = f x Dose` |
| Shared V, kCP, kPC for both forms | yes | yes | Methods assumption 4 and the V definition |

# Simulation

Table 2 and Figure 6 of the paper simulate one IV dose at several initial
attribute levels over 42 days. The paper does not state the simulated dose,
so it is recovered from Table 2: the total-MAB2 AUC from day 0 to 42 of the
deamidation model is 209.7 h x mg/mL, which is 8737.5 day x mg/L. Because
the model is linear, the dose is that AUC divided by the AUC per mg.

```{r scenarios}
grid <- sort(unique(c(0, 10 / 1440, 1 / 24, 4 / 24, 0.5, seq(0, 42, by = 0.05))))

simulate_level <- function(mod, attribute, level_pct, dose) {
  cmt_mod <- paste0("central_", attribute)
  par <- setNames(level_pct / 100, paste0("fdose_", attribute))
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "central", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = cmt_mod, time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(grid, cmt = "central")
  sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = par))
  sim |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      attribute = attribute,
      level_pct = level_pct,
      time,
      Cc,
      Cc_attr = .data[[paste0("Cc_", attribute)]],
      pct_attr = .data[[paste0("pct_", attribute)]]
    )
}

auc_0_42 <- function(sim, conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, Cc = .data[[conc_col]]) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))
  o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | id)
  o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    o_conc,
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 42, auclast = TRUE)
  )
  res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data))
  res$PPORRES[res$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
}

# Dose anchor: total-MAB2 AUC(0-42) of the deamidation model at a 1 mg dose
auc_per_mg <- auc_0_42(simulate_level(mod_deamid, "deamid", 0, 1), "Cc")
published_total_auc <- 209.7 * 1000 / 24 # h x mg/mL -> day x mg/L
dose_mg <- published_total_auc / auc_per_mg
dose_mg
```

The recovered dose is about `r signif(dose_mg / 1000, 3)` g. It is used for
every simulation below, of both models, so the only Table 2 cell used to set
it is the deamidation 0% total AUC; every other cell is a check.

```{r simulate}
deamid_levels <- c(0, 5.6, 11.2, 16.7, 27.8, 100)
man5_levels <- c(0, 3.0, 6.0, 8.9, 14.9, 100)

sims <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(deamid_levels, function(x) simulate_level(mod_deamid, "deamid", x, dose_mg)),
  lapply(man5_levels, function(x) simulate_level(mod_man5, "man5", x, dose_mg))
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 6: concentration of the modified form

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 6 of Li 2016: concentration (ng/mL) of the deamidated
# (A) and the Man5 (B) MAB2 form after one IV dose at several initial levels.
fig6 <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, !(attribute == "man5" & level_pct == 0)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel = ifelse(attribute == "deamid", "A) Deamidation", "B) Man5"),
    level = factor(paste0(sprintf("%.1f", level_pct), "%"),
      levels = unique(paste0(sprintf("%.1f", sort(unique(level_pct))), "%"))
    )
  )
ggplot(fig6, aes(time, Cc_attr * 1000, colour = level)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1e7)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = "Initial level",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Li 2016."
  )
```

As in the paper, the deamidated form accumulates even when none is in the
dose (the 0% curve rises to roughly 2 x 10^4 ng/mL and stays there), and the
curves for the different initial levels converge over 42 days because
conversion, not the initial level, dominates. The Man5 curves stay
proportional to the initial level, since Man5 is not formed in circulation.

## Figure 4: relative attribute level over time

Figure 4 plots the relative level of each attribute in the three patients.
The values below were digitised by the maintainers from Figure 4A and 4B as
the approximate mean of the three patients at each sampling day (read to
about 1 percentage point for deamidation and 0.1 point for Man5).

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 4A and 4B of Li 2016 with the clinical-batch levels.
fig4_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~attribute, ~time, ~pct_obs,
  "deamid", 0, 5.5,
  "deamid", 2, 6.2,
  "deamid", 4, 8.7,
  "deamid", 7, 12.0,
  "deamid", 14, 18.8,
  "deamid", 21, 25.0,
  "deamid", 42, 36.0,
  "man5", 0, 2.9,
  "man5", 2, 2.3,
  "man5", 4, 1.7,
  "man5", 7, 1.37,
  "man5", 14, 1.03,
  "man5", 21, 0.88,
  "man5", 42, 0.53
)
batch <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(
    (attribute == "deamid" & level_pct == 5.6) |
      (attribute == "man5" & level_pct == 3.0)
  )
ggplot(batch, aes(time, pct_attr)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4_obs, aes(y = pct_obs), shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~attribute, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Relative level (%)",
    caption = "Line: model. Points: digitised mean of Figure 4 of Li 2016."
  )

fig4_cmp <- fig4_obs |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    batch |>
      dplyr::transmute(attribute, time = round(time, 6), pct_model = pct_attr),
    by = c("attribute", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff_points = pct_model - pct_obs)
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Attribute" = attribute,
    "Day" = time,
    "Figure 4 (%)" = pct_obs,
    "Model (%)" = pct_model,
    "Model - figure (points)" = diff_points
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(fig4_cmp$pct_model),
  # Deterministic model against figure readings: within the reading accuracy
  # plus the fit residual of a three-patient mean.
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$diff_points[fig4_cmp$attribute == "deamid"]) < 3),
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$diff_points[fig4_cmp$attribute == "man5"]) < 0.4)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 2 reports, for each initial level, the AUC from day 0 to 42 of the
modified form ("attribute AUC") and of total MAB2, and their ratio. Both
AUCs are computed here with PKNCA from the simulated profiles.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sims |>
  dplyr::filter(level_pct < 100) |>
  dplyr::select(attribute, level_pct, time, total = Cc, modified = Cc_attr) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(total, modified), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = paste0(attribute, " ", sprintf("%.1f", level_pct), "% | ", analyte)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(factor(treatment)))

# Every profile has a post-dose time-zero row from the observation grid.
stopifnot(all(tapply(nca_input$time, nca_input$id, min) == 0))

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  nca_input |> dplyr::distinct(treatment, id) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 42, auclast = TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)
```

## Comparison against Table 2

```{r nca-compare}
# Table 2 of Li 2016, converted from h x mg/mL to day x mg/L (x 1000 / 24).
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~attribute, ~level_pct, ~modified, ~total, ~relative,
  "deamid", 0.0, 21.9, 209.7, 10.5,
  "deamid", 5.6, 32.4, 209.7, 15.4,
  "deamid", 11.2, 42.8, 209.7, 20.4,
  "deamid", 27.8, 74.2, 209.7, 35.4,
  "man5", 0.0, 0.0, 212.8, 0.0,
  "man5", 3.0, 3.2, 209.6, 1.5,
  "man5", 6.0, 6.4, 206.4, 3.1,
  "man5", 14.9, 15.9, 196.9, 8.1
)
published <- table2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(modified, total), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "auc_h_mg_ml") |>
  dplyr::filter(auc_h_mg_ml > 0) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    treatment = paste0(attribute, " ", sprintf("%.1f", level_pct), "% | ", analyte),
    auclast = auc_h_mg_ml * 1000 / 24
  )

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "day*mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "AUC(0-42 day): Table 2 of Li 2016 vs. simulated. * differs by >20%.",
  digits = 1
)

# Typical-value solve against the published typical-value simulation, so a
# tight bound on every row is appropriate.
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, auc_sim = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim / auclast - 1))
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_chk) == nrow(published),
  all(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff) < 3)
)
max(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff))
```

Every row agrees within 3% (the largest difference is printed above). The deamidation total-AUC rows are not
an independent check (the deamidation 0% total sets the dose, and the total
does not depend on the initial level when both forms clear at the same rate),
but the Man5 totals, including the Man5 0% row, and every attribute AUC are.

```{r relative-auc}
# Relative AUC = attribute AUC / total AUC x 100 (Table 2, last column, as
# printed).
# Dose-independent, so it checks the model without the dose anchor.
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::separate(treatment, c("scenario", "analyte"), sep = " \\| ") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(relative_sim = 100 * modified / total)

rel <- table2 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    scenario = paste0(attribute, " ", sprintf("%.1f", level_pct), "%"),
    relative_pub = relative
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_auc |> dplyr::select(scenario, relative_sim), by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff_points = relative_sim - relative_pub)
rel |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Table 2 relative AUC (%)" = relative_pub,
    "Simulated relative AUC (%)" = relative_sim,
    "Difference (points)" = diff_points
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(rel$relative_sim),
  # The deterministic model reproduces the Man5 column to its printed digit
  # and the deamidation column to within the rounding of ktr (printed 0.01).
  all(abs(rel$diff_points) < 0.5)
)
```

The Man5 relative AUCs match Table 2 to the printed digit. The deamidation
relative AUCs run 0.1-0.3 percentage points below Table 2, consistently
across levels; Table 1 prints the conversion rate constant `ktr` to one
significant figure (0.01 /day), and the unrounded estimate that produced
Table 2 is not reported.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose.** The paper does not report the MAB2 dose ("a single high dose").
  The dose used in the simulations (about `r signif(dose_mg / 1000, 3)` g)
  is back-solved from the deamidation 0% total AUC of Table 2. It is
  consistent with the start of the 100% curve in Figure 6 (dose / V of about
  1.4 x 10^6 ng/mL) and with the Man5 0% total AUC, which it reproduces
  independently. The model files declare doses in mg and do not depend on
  this value.
- **AUC units.** Table 2 labels its AUCs "h x mg/mL". With the recovered
  dose that label is consistent with Figure 6, and the values were converted
  to day x mg/L (x 1000 / 24) for comparison.
- **Initial levels.** `fdose_deamid = 0.056` and `fdose_man5 = 0.030` are
  the lowest non-zero initial levels of Table 2 and Figure 6; the other
  levels are 2, 3 and 5 times these, and the day-0 levels in Figure 4 (about
  5.5% and 2.9%) agree, so they are taken to be the levels of the clinical
  batch. The paper does not print the batch levels as model parameters.
- **No between-subject variability or residual error.** Table 1 reports CVs
  of the parameter estimates only, and no error model is given, so both
  models are typical-value models.
- **Deamidated-form clearance.** Table 1 prints `kclmod` = 0.13 /day with the
  same CV as `kcl0`, which is Methods assumption 1 (`kclmod = kcl0`); the
  model therefore computes `kel_deamid <- kel` instead of carrying a separate
  estimate.
- **Man5 conversion.** With `ktr = 0` (Table 1; Methods assumption 2) the
  Man5 model has no conversion term, so the Man5 and Man5-free forms are two
  independent two-compartment models that share V, kCP and kPC.
- **Peripheral conversion.** Equations 2 and 4 and Figure 5 include
  conversion of the original form in the peripheral compartment at the same
  rate constant as in the central compartment; the deamidation model keeps
  it.
- **Concentrations.** `Cc` is total MAB2 (both forms), `Cc_deamid` /
  `Cc_man5` the modified form, and `pct_deamid` / `pct_man5` the modified
  form as a percentage of total MAB2, the quantity Figure 4 plots. Before
  the first dose the percentage is undefined (0 / 0).
- No correction notice for the article was found in PubMed (checked
  2026-11-24).
